architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Let delta be the directly measured percentage change in the 120-130 C viscosity level of S1C41 relative to the matched unmodified reactive-core reference. Accept exactly one formulation-level hypothesis if delta is within 3.4 percentage points of its registered prediction: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.7567%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.2433%, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.7567%. The result must be reported as a combined-composition level result, not as axis-specific attribution.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The 120-130 C viscosity level is measured directly in the selected resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry, so the primary decision observable does not depend on transferring a rheological regularity measured in the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family. The E_eta comparison with the prior shared shape is outside that validated chemistry support and is diagnostic only; it cannot be used as a reconstruction shortcut or as evidence of molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the directly measured delta differs from -42.7567% by more than 3.4 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if delta is at or below -42.7567%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if delta is at or above -42.7567%. A result outside all three 3.4-percentage-point acceptance bands falsifies the registered predictive assignment for this experiment without establishing a molecular mechanism. The nominal 3.4-point boundary is conditional on repeatability and process-state variation being sufficiently controlled; otherwise the result is indeterminate rather than chemical falsification.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 with at least two independent repeats to measure the unresolved 120 C isothermal drift directly; retain fully recorded preparation and thermal histories. If axis-specific attribution remains required, subsequently run matched single-axis acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like candidates.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the 120 and 130 C processing-window temperatures, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 is within the externally supported dual-axis intervention region and gives large separation among the registered formulation-level level predictions. M-SWEEP is the scientifically defensible card because it directly observes the 120-130 C processing-window level rather than reconstructing it from an unverified shared shape. It tests the level hypotheses and candidate-specific thermal response, while making no molecular-mechanism claim. The experiment does not by itself establish mitigation of the identified hot-hold failure mode; that requires the separate M-HOLD-120 measurement.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-SWEEP because it directly measures the decision-temperature level in the unvalidated modified chemistry and avoids the audit-flagged M-ANCHOR shortcut. I followed the Skeptic on the limitations: the dual-axis formulation leaves attribution entangled, the 3.4% threshold is not demonstrated for this candidate with one repeat, and hot-hold drift remains unresolved. The advisory audit marks the competing M-ANCHOR cards inadmissible before shape verification, and I therefore reject their deterministic ranking despite the audit being non-binding.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The selected dual-axis composition changes AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, so the measured level can test combined-composition predictions but cannot isolate acrylic-like, tackifier-like, or interaction effects.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the directly measured 80-130 C viscosity levels, but high for any inference that the unmodified-family shared thermal shape transfers to S1C41 or that E_eta similarity implies chemical equivalence.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The M-SWEEP catalog resolution is 3.4%, based on prior direct-sweep residuals; this is a nominal resolution, not a candidate-specific repeatability estimate.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Substantial because the sweep does not itself control preparation-state variation; the one-repeat card cannot reliably distinguish a small chemical deviation from uncontrolled realization variation.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original reactive polyurethane hot-melt family around the E1-E3 reactive-core formulations, including the separately verified E1 +P chemical perturbation; the local evidence does not establish support for an unregistered chemistry-changing modifier. A direct temperature sweep and matched-window hold would stay inside the measured protocol and chemistry support only if the intended candidate remains within that audited family; otherwise the chemistry-domain gate must require direct verification rather than one-point shape transfer.
planner.failure_mode: Unresolved isothermal thermal-hold instability of the modified reactive polyurethane melt, with possible large viscosity drift during residence at application temperature.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: At 120 C, the original E5 hold showed SI_15_to_60 = 0.515 and SI_15_to_90 = 0.931, much larger than E1, which showed 0.095 and 0.168 over the same intervals.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local temperature response has six-point sweeps for E1, E2, and E3, with three E2 runs at each temperature, whereas the isothermal trajectory is represented by only one original hold for E1 and one for E5, with no modified-candidate hold profile. The large E1-E5 contrast therefore establishes the risk but does not resolve the candidate-specific time behavior.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate viscosity directly from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample, including the 120 and 130 C decision temperatures, and report the apparent temperature-response descriptor from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

Compare the measured level with the declared inert-dilution prediction at matched temperature with sufficient repeatability to distinguish above-dilution, at-dilution, and below-dilution outcomes using the registered resolution.

Hold the melt at 120 C and record viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min in at least two independent repeats, reporting SI_15_to_60; extend to 90 min if the longer residence trajectory is required for comparison with the local E1 and E5 evidence.
Record preparation and thermal history so a level or drift difference can be separated from uncontrolled realization-state variation.
planner.scientific_question: For a registered modified candidate, does the realized viscosity level across the measured 80-130 C range follow inert dilution, rise above inert dilution as predicted by acrylic association, or fall below it as predicted by plasticization, and does its directly measured temperature response remain compatible with the local shared shape rather than masking a chemistry-dependent failure?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The primary processing-window level is measured directly, so it does not depend on transferring the shared thermal-response shape into the resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry. The candidate chemistry itself remains outside the family in which the local shared shape was validated; therefore the sweep is appropriate as direct chemistry-specific verification, while any shared-shape comparison is diagnostic rather than an admissible reconstruction shortcut.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the directly measured 120-130 C level change relative to the unmodified reactive core falls within the M-SWEEP resolution of 3.4% of exactly one registered prediction—-42.7567% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.2433% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.7567% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC—that hypothesis is accepted for S1C41 and the directly measured processing-window level is reported with it.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -42.7567% by more than 3.4%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level is at or below -42.7567%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.7567%.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result that does not fall within 3.4% of one prediction, or cannot distinguish predictions because of repeatability or realization-state variation, does not support a unique registered level hypothesis. The candidate's direct temperature response remains characterized, but additional controlled repeats or a follow-up measurement would be needed.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the 120 and 130 C processing-window temperatures, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the deterministic top VOI, but its 120-130 C observable is reconstructed from a single 110 C anchor using a shared shape not verified for the candidate chemistry, and the audit marks it inadmissible_before_shape_verification.

It directly addresses the planner's unresolved isothermal drift coordinate, but it does not return the processing-window level and cannot separate the three registered level hypotheses; its decision relevance is only 0.25.

It characterizes between-preparation state spread but does not directly determine the candidate's processing-window level or discriminate the registered level hypotheses, and it has the highest declared effort.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41 is inside the externally supported dual-axis intervention region at 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, with all three level hypotheses separated by large predicted differences. M-SWEEP is the scientifically safer measurement because it directly observes the 120-130 C decision quantity in the unvalidated modified chemistry rather than inferring it from an unverified local shape. It also provides the candidate-specific temperature response needed to test whether shape transfer is reasonable.
proposer.tie_break_justification: The deterministic top tie consists of M-ANCHOR cards with identical VOI components, but each reconstructs the decision-temperature level through an unverified shared shape and is marked inadmissible_before_shape_verification by the chemistry audit. M-SWEEP is slightly lower in deterministic VOI but measures the decision quantity directly, verifies the candidate-specific thermal response, and avoids chemistry-dependent shape extrapolation.

robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal departs from the deterministic tied top set, which consists of inadmissible M-ANCHOR cards for S1C41, S1C46, S1C51, S1C56, and S1C61. The departure is scientifically justified because M-SWEEP directly measures the 120-130 C decision quantity in the resin-modified chemistry, whereas M-ANCHOR reconstructs it using a shared shape with no verified transfer to that chemistry.
residual_decision_risk: The dual-axis S1C41 composition cannot isolate acrylic-like effects from minor-tackifier-like effects or their interaction.
Candidate-specific repeatability and realization-state variation may exceed the nominal 3.4% M-SWEEP residual.
M-SWEEP does not measure the 120 C isothermal hold trajectory, so candidate-specific thermal-hold drift remains unresolved.

The resin-modified chemistry remains outside the measured shared-shape support; E_eta comparison and any shape-transfer claim are diagnostic only until direct verification establishes transferability.
The registered level hypotheses are formulation-level comparisons and do not establish molecular association, plasticization, or other mechanisms.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that the 3.4% M-SWEEP threshold is not supported for S1C41 by a one-repeat protocol with substantial process-state risk and no candidate-specific repeatability estimate. This weakens the proposed acceptance and falsification interpretation, but it does not change which measurement should be run: M-SWEEP still directly observes the processing-window level. At least two independent preparations with fully recorded process and thermal histories are needed before applying a threshold-based hypothesis decision. The separate unresolved 120 C hold trajectory also remains a residual limitation rather than a reason to replace the direct sweep for the primary level question.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No tested perturbation changes the deterministic tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the intervention-family and measurement-plan stabilities are both 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survives the entire 0.5-1.5 multiplier sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.002292. These perturbations are defensible sensitivity checks for the transparent score, but they do not make the M-ANCHOR observable scientifically admissible or repair its unsupported chemistry transfer.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable is not inside the previously measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry support because S1C41 is resin_modified:ac1920+tk100. The proposal correctly uses M-SWEEP rather than M-ANCHOR to obtain the 120-130 C level directly. A direct candidate-specific sweep is required before any shared-shape transfer can be treated as verified; the sweep's E_eta comparison remains diagnostic until that verification is established.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The numerical predictions are separated by much more than the nominal 3.4% M-SWEEP residual, but the protocol does not establish that 3.4% is the resolution for S1C41. With one repeat, no explicit matched unmodified reference repeat, and six missing process fields reflected in process_state_risk 0.75, preparation and realization variation can exceed the declared threshold. The criterion is therefore not practically attainable as a defensible falsification test without replication and controlled process-history recording.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can support only a formulation-level prediction for the combined S1C41 composition, not the claimed axis-specific acrylic-association or plasticization interpretation.
objections.objection: The three registered level predictions for S1C41 are numerically separated at the declared M-SWEEP resolution: -42.7567% versus 17.2433% versus -72.7567%, with the closest pair 30 percentage points apart and a 3.4% M-SWEEP threshold. However, the experiment uses only one dual-axis composition, so it cannot determine whether an apparent elevation or depression is caused by the acrylic-like axis, the minor-tackifier-like axis, or their interaction. The proposer declares no hypotheses as unseparated and does not admit this attribution limitation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result above or below the dilution prediction could be incorrectly attributed to acrylic association or to a plasticizing continuum when the measured effect could instead arise from TK100, AC1920, or their interaction.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes AC1920 to 15.0% and TK100 to 5.0% simultaneously, while reducing the reactive core to a reactive mass fraction of 0.8. Because both modifier axes move together, the primary level change cannot isolate acrylic association from tackifier plasticization or an interaction between them. The registered H-LEVEL-ASSOC depends on the acrylic_like axis, whereas H-LEVEL-PLASTIC depends on the sum of both axes; one dual-axis observation does not identify either axis effect.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Only the interpretation of E_eta and any shared-shape comparison would be weakened; the directly measured 120-130 C level itself remains interpretable.
objections.objection: The selected M-SWEEP protocol measures viscosity directly from 80 to 130 C, including the 120 and 130 C decision temperatures, so the primary processing-window level is direct rather than reconstructed. The accompanying E_eta descriptor from regression of ln(eta) versus 1/T is model-dependent, but it is not necessary for the primary level decision.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A compatible-looking sweep could be overinterpreted as validation of shape transfer or local-family interpolation, despite the absence of prior verified support for resin-modified chemistry.
objections.objection: S1C41 is in chemistry family resin_modified:ac1920+tk100, while the shared thermal-response shape was measured only for unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI. The audit therefore marks this chemistry modified_chemistry_unvalidated, has_prior_verified_shape_transfer false, and shared_shape_use verification_only. M-SWEEP appropriately measures the modified chemistry directly, but any claim that the candidate remains compatible with the prior shared shape is diagnostic only and cannot be used as prior support for the primary level.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A single S1C41 result cannot reliably establish that a deviation greater than 3.4% is chemical falsification rather than realization-state or preparation variability; the stated acceptance and falsification boundaries are therefore not attainable as specified.
objections.objection: The falsification criterion relies on the M-SWEEP resolution of 3.4%, but the protocol specifies min_repeats: 1 and does not provide a candidate-specific repeatability estimate. The 3.4% value is the residual of a shared-shape plus intercept-only fit to prior direct sweeps, not demonstrated measurement or preparation-state uncertainty for S1C41. The local one-point validation reports pooled errors of roughly 6-10%, and the proposed card assigns process_state_risk 0.75 with six missing process fields.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may discriminate static level hypotheses while leaving candidate-specific thermal-hold instability entirely unresolved; it cannot support a claim that the modified candidate mitigates the identified processing failure.
objections.objection: The planner identifies unresolved isothermal time behavior as the least-resolved coordinate and documents large E1-E5 hold contrast: SI_15_to_60 of 0.095 versus 0.515. M-SWEEP measures static temperature response only and has no hold segment, whereas M-HOLD-120 is the catalog measurement that directly observes the 15-60 minute drift. The proposer selects M-SWEEP without adding the hold required to test the stated hot-hold failure mode.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be reported as evidence for molecular association or plasticization even though the planned rheology only supports an empirical level comparison.
objections.objection: The rheological sweep can test level and temperature-response compatibility but cannot establish a molecular association mechanism, a plasticizing continuum mechanism, or lower effective reactive-group density. The registry explicitly bounds the hypotheses as formulation-level statements and states that none asserts a molecular association mechanism. Any interpretation of M-SWEEP as mechanistic confirmation would exceed the measurement scope.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct 80-130 C M-SWEEP, but require at least two independent S1C41 preparations with fully recorded process and thermal histories and estimate repeatability before applying the 3.4% criterion. Add the payload's M-HOLD-120 protocol with at least two repeats to address the unresolved 120 C drift coordinate. If axis-specific attribution is required, add matched single-axis acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like compositions rather than relying on the confounded dual-axis point.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 3.4% falsification threshold is not supported by the specified protocol: M-SWEEP has min_repeats 1, while the candidate has substantial process-state risk and the available local anchor validation shows roughly 6-10% pooled error. Thus the experiment may directly measure the level but cannot reliably decide whether deviations from -42.7567%, 17.2433%, or -72.7567% exceed the declared resolution.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
